column1: # Countries (Wikidata citizenship, P27) and the languages their people's names are in, as language/espeak voice.
# Claude's picks, for Brendan to review. A country of one language is evidence that its people's names are in it,
# and one dominated by one language is listed with that one (Finland, Canada). One listed with several (Belgium,
# Switzerland, the Austro-Hungarian and Russian empires) is no evidence either way: its citizenship can't tell a
# Flemish name from a Walloon one. A citizenship with no languages here (scripts other than Latin, countries too
# small to list) is evidence against every language. English-speaking countries are en: a name their people
# mostly bear is read as English reads it.
